source.title: A behavioural correlate of the synaptic eligibility trace in the nucleus accumbens.

confidence_rationale: Behavioural + optogenetic confirmation that the ~1s NAc synaptic eligibility-trace window governs a reward-sensitive period -- bridges the synaptic mechanism (Brzosko) to behaviour and to biologically plausible RL eligibility traces. Mid confidence: NAc Pavlovian reward, not rule-level credit.
failure_signatures: The reward-sensitive window is ~1s and tied to NAc presynaptic activity for a sensorimotor event -- ARC-063 rule-evidence traces are presumed to operate over much longer, rule-relevant horizons, a timescale gap this paper does not address.
Establishes credit timing for a sensorimotor cue->reward association, not for a rule that organised the behaviour.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In head-fixed Pavlovian conditioning, the reward-sensitive period for a brief tone is within ~1s of the tone and depends on plasticity-related signalling in the nucleus accumbens, matching the synaptic eligibility-trace window measured in slices -- supporting application of the synaptic eligibility trace to biologically plausible RL models.
mapping.ree_translation: Behavioural confirmation that the eligibility-trace credit mechanism (entry brzosko2015) is real at the behavioural level and governs WHEN an outcome can credit a preceding event. ARC-063's evidence-trace credit assumes such a creditable window exists; this paper shows it does and that it is plasticity-gated in a reward hub.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The window is ~1s and tied to a sensorimotor cue in the NAc; ARC-063 needs credit over rule-relevant horizons and to a rule object. The paper grounds the EXISTENCE and plasticity-dependence of an eligibility window, not its rule-level or long-horizon form.
mapping.source_context: Mouse head-fixed Pavlovian conditioning with optogenetic NAc presynaptic stimulation.

confidence_components.notes: Solid behavioural-optogenetic paper; companion to Brzosko. Discounted for timescale + rule-target gaps.
